executive_assessment.text: Dated flood and drought impacts distinguish Ourika, Guelmim, Gharb, Haouz, Saïss, Agadir and Oriental; national displacement totals must not be assigned to those places.
Water-dependent rural and fisheries livelihoods face differentiated pressures; migration-related plans and modeled labor losses do not establish violence.

Regional and community plans provide capacities, while the Oriental project mission documents implementation delays and Amejjaou drainage weaknesses. Activities and targets are not demonstrated outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025 reports: 2022-23 deficits reached 81% in unnamed basins and cereal output fell 67%; the NDC records 50.4°C heat in Agadir and over 6,000 hectares burned in Oriental in 2023.

The NDC reports historical flood deaths at Ourika in 1995 and Guelmim in 2014, and a separate national total of nearly 22,000 internal displacements in 2008-2024. That displacement total is not assigned to these cities or particular flood events.

The NDC reports drought-related fruit losses in Gharb, Haouz and Saïss in 2022 and disproportionate livelihood pressure on rural women. Its discussion links farm precarity with rural out-migration; it does not establish violence or allocate migration counts to these regions.
Source dated 2025 reports: Regional plans in Oriental, Drâa-Tafilalet, Souss-Massa, Béni Mellal-Khénifra and Marrakech-Safi target oasis and rural adaptation.

Source dated 2022-01 reports: The plan reports 1960-2018 rainfall decline, warming and increased aridity; southern and southeast Atlas provinces are arid, while Souss, El Haouz and Oriental include semi-arid zones.

Source dated 2022-01 reports: By 2050, catch potential could fall 5% under RCP8.5; artisanal fishers, small aquaculture producers and women-majority fish processors are identified as especially exposed.
Source dated 2022-01 reports: The plan proposes oasis livelihood diversification and climate early warning, and community-led vulnerability mapping and water options tailored to each mountain massif.

Source dated 2026-02-05 reports: The 2025 mission found cumulative delays, 9% effective physical execution and under 1% disbursement; it attributed slow progress partly to limited provincial agriculture-department capacity and delayed technical assistance.
Source dated 2026-02-05 reports: The report records 5,651 activity participants, 45% women and 52% youth, against design targets of 30% and 40%; another section gives a different reach total.

Source dated 2026-02-05 reports: Strong recent floods damaged the provisionally accepted Amejjaou track in Driouch; missing drainage and slope protections leave its durability at risk under intensifying extreme rainfall.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 13 of 13 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

The reviewed primary sources document climate-related displacement, rural migration pathways and gendered livelihood pressures, but none establishes armed conflict, organized violence or insecurity as a climate mediator in Morocco.
The NDC's 2026-2035 mobility-reduction measures are planned benefits, not measured migration outcomes; national displacement totals are not allocated to specific events or localities.
The World Bank water and labor estimates are 2020 model scenarios based on a 2016 baseline, not observed subnational impacts or current employment conditions.
IFAD's project supervision reflects a November 2025 mission. Its reported beneficiary reach differs across sections, so the discrepancy is retained rather than reconciled by assumption.

Climate-related displacement and possible livelihood-mediated migration are documented or modeled, but do not by themselves establish violence or fragility. No complete mediated violence or reverse-FCV chain was verified.
The 2020 comparative-static water model is scenario-based and national; its employment and migration discussion is not an observed local effect.
IFAD's February 2026 report reflects a November 2025 mission. Reach totals differ between sections and participation figures are outputs, not evaluated resilience impacts.
